paragraphs: OffenderWatch sells sex offender registry software to law enforcement agencies, hosted so records can be shared between jurisdictions and published to the public. The company says it works in partnership with more than 15,000 law enforcement officers, agency staff, and community members, and that the software monitors hundreds of thousands of sex offenders nationwide. The site describes the product as a configurable SOR monitoring platform that agencies use to improve efficiency and maintain compliance.

Agencies named on the site include Oklahoma City Police Department and Corpus Christi Police Department, with testimonials attributed to Sedgwick County, KS and Wakulla County, FL. Officers quoted there describe running statewide or nationwide investigative searches and sharing offender records with other agencies within minutes. The site also lists a Family Safety App for the public, alongside FAQs and a page on talking to children about sex offenders. The company states that the platform is backed by over 25 years of expertise and is built for public safety.

quote.text: In partnership with more than 15,000 law enforcement officers, agency staff, and community members, OffenderWatch® helps monitor hundreds of thousands of sex offenders nationwide.
